question:
An 18-year-old African-American woman comes to the physician for the evaluation of worsening fatigue that started 1 year ago. Physical examination shows mild jaundice and splenomegaly. Laboratory studies show:
Hemoglobin 10.4 g/dL
Mean corpuscular hemoglobin concentration 43% Hb/cell
Platelet count 220,000/mm3
Reticulocyte count 7%
A peripheral blood smear shows target cells and erythrocytes with hemoglobin crystals. Which of the following is the most likely underlying cause of this patient's findings?"?

options.opa: Replacement of glutamate by valine in beta-globin chain
options.opb: Decreased conversion of oxidized glutathione into its reduced form
options.opc: Replacement of glutamate by lysine in beta-globin chain
options.opd: Reduced production of beta-globin due to a mutation in the HbB gene
options.ope: Acquired mutation of membrane-bound glycosylphosphatidylinositol anchor

analysis: The patient's presentation with worsening fatigue, mild jaundice, splenomegaly, anemia, target cells, and erythrocytes with hemoglobin crystals is indicative of hemolytic anemia. The presence of target cells suggests membrane abnormalities, which are characteristic of sickle cell disease. The replacement of glutamate by valine in the beta-globin chain is the specific mutation seen in sickle cell disease.
